chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you buy your sacrificial animal (Udhiyah) and wrap it, and it is placed beside your saddle, the Hady (sacrificial animal for Hajj) has reached its designated place; so if you wish to shave [your head], then shave.

key_terms.قَمَطَ: To wrap or bind the animal
key_terms.مَحِلّ: Designated place or time for a ritual act

ai.seo_question: When is a pilgrim allowed to shave their head after sacrificing the Hady during Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar, this hadith clarifies the precise moment the Hady (sacrificial animal) attains its ritual status, marking the threshold for the pilgrim's release from Ihram restrictions. It establishes that the act of purchasing, wrapping, and positioning the animal beside the saddle constitutes the completion of the Hady's preparation, thereby permitting the pilgrim to shave their head (Halaq) even before the actual slaughter occurs. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the preparatory acts as sufficient for the transition of ritual state.
